Advance 2 seconds to elect the leader. In the Database tab, follow the quorum lab and propose a write on the leader. A commit requires a response from a majority over the model's actual cables. Disconnect both of the leader's cables: it may still consider itself the leader, but it cannot commit new writes. The two remaining replicas elect another leader. Reconnect the cables to reconcile the uncommitted history. The committed local copy is historical; it does not certify a current read. This study store is independent of the SQL database and the other services. Committed prefixes are compacted automatically; up to 256 retained entries, 128 uncommitted entries and 512 KiB per checkpoint, with no membership changes. The consensus channel has no vendor PCAP codec.

Start the simulation to complete DAD and SLAAC. In the IPv6 tab, copy the address of PC-V6-B and ping it from PC-V6-A. A Hop Limit of 1 reveals R-IPV6. Reduce the outbound MTU to 1280 and send 1400 bytes to observe Packet Too Big. RA and NDP use multicast on the local link.

Advance to negotiate LACP and converge RSTP. SW-A in active mode initiates the exchange; SW-B in passive mode responds. STP sees Port-channel1 as a single link. Shut down Gi0/1 on SW-A and repeat ping/HTTP over the remaining Gi0/2. Configure min-links 2 to suspend the group if only one member remains.

Shut down Gi0/2 or disconnect its cable on R-PRIMARY. The effective priority drops from 150 to 70, below the 100 of R-BACKUP. Advance the simulation and repeat ping/HTTP. R-PRIMARY stays powered on. When the uplink recovers, preempt returns the role to the primary.

R-01/02/03 belong to AS 65001/65002/65003. Advance to establish BGP over TCP/179. R-01 prefers AS_PATH 65003; shutdown on Gi0/2 forces the path via 65002 65003. Adjust LOCAL_PREF to apply policy, inspect OPEN/UPDATE and validate ping/HTTP. A 9 s hold time is chosen for the lab; engine default: 90 s.

The virtual gateways are 192.168.10.1 and 192.168.20.1. R-PRIMARY starts as ACTIVE (150); R-BACKUP stays BACKUP (100). Run ping/HTTP from PC-01 to WEB-01, power off R-PRIMARY and advance 4 s. Repeat the traffic and check the virtual MAC in ARP. When R-PRIMARY is powered back on, preempt returns the role to the primary. Backup static routes only cover an administrative shutdown of a single port. NAT/firewall sessions are not replicated.

PC-01 can access HTTP on the WAN (192.168.20.10) and in the DMZ (192.168.30.10). WAN-CLIENT can access only HTTP/80 in the DMZ; ping and echo/7 are blocked, as are connections to the LAN. On PC-01, traceroute 192.168.20.10 shows the TTL error traversing PAT and the firewall. Inspect the ICMP quoted headers and change rules in Policies.
